runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Generated poteto-mode, feature, and how Skills plus implementer TOML committed in a disposable Git fixture; worktrees feature enabled; root ran in a managed worktree; project rules ignored; base user configuration loaded because this CLI surface requires it for the authenticated run.
runtime.permissionProfile: workspace-write sandbox in a managed root worktree with one serialized bounded writer

assertions.evidence: The root explicitly loaded the repository-generated poteto-mode router.
The root read only the generated repository Skills, role definition, request, and project files; no external Skill or plugin cache participated.
The router selected feature because the request intentionally added optional receipt-note behavior.
The root loaded feature and followed how's simple root inspection path over createReceipt, normalization, rendering, and tests.
Before delegation the root read the entry point, both implementation modules, and the test and identified normalization as the input boundary.
The root selected frozen { customer, note, items }, recorded empty-string omission semantics, and explained why the specified behavior needed no prototype or panel.
The root recorded the failing-test gate, shared two-file data contract, lack of independent slices, and one writer as the smallest safe decomposition.
Before spawning the writer, the root ran node --test test/receipt.test.mjs and captured exit 1 with one pass and one missing-note failure.
Exactly one receipt_note child thread ran, with no retry or replacement.
The inline implementer contract permitted only normalize-order.mjs and receipt.mjs, and the child changed exactly those files.
The root ran in a managed worktree isolated from the original fixture; because nested child isolation was unavailable, exactly one child wrote serially inside that worktree.
The root independently ran git diff --check, inspected the actual two-file diff, reread both implementations and index.mjs, and rejected no unrelated paths.
The root reran the exact command after the child completed and captured exit 0 with two passing tests.
The missing and whitespace-only note cases retained the original customer and items output.
Only the two allowed implementation files changed in the managed worktree; the original fixture stayed at its committed source hashes.
The run made no commit, push, publication, or pull-request operation.

limitations: The generated implementer role was not selectable on this CLI spawn surface, so its bounded contract was supplied inline.

The final response described nested child isolation as unavailable but omitted that the entire root session already ran in a managed worktree; the persisted session metadata and original-repository hashes establish that outer isolation.
The supplied behavioral test does not exercise a non-string note; the root disclosed that boundary.
Unrelated configured MCP startup and authentication warnings did not participate in the workflow.
